sections.summary: Dijkstra argues that human minds are geared to static relations, not dynamic processes, so programs should minimize the conceptual gap between text and process. He introduces textual and dynamic indices as coordinates for process progress, explains why go to statements destroy any meaningful independent coordinate system, and concludes that the go to statement is too primitive and should be abolished from higher-level languages.
sections.title: The Case Against the Go To Statement
